passages.text: After this, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.
passages.sermon: Paul was a Christian preacher and apostle.\r\nPaul left the city of Athens.\r\nPaul went to the city of Corinth.
passages.original: Μετὰ ταῦτα χωρισθεὶς ἐκ τῶν Ἀθηνῶν ἦλθεν εἰς Κόρινθον

passages.text: There he found a Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome. Paul went to visit them, and he stayed and worked with them because they were tentmakers by trade, just as he was.
passages.sermon:
Paul arrived in Corinth.
He found a Jew named Aquila.
Aquila was from Pontus.
Aquila had recently come from Italy.
Aquila’s wife was Priscilla.
Claudius, the Roman emperor, had ordered all Jews to leave Rome.
Aquila and Priscilla left Rome because of this order.
Paul went to visit Aquila and Priscilla.
Paul stayed with them.
Paul worked with them.
Paul, Aquila, and Priscilla were tentmakers by trade.
passages.original: καὶ εὑρών τινα Ἰουδαῖον ὀνόματι Ἀκύλαν Ποντικὸν τῷ γένει προσφάτως ἐληλυθότα ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰταλίας καὶ Πρίσκιλλαν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ διὰ τὸ διατεταχέναι Κλαύδιον χωρίζεσθαι πάντας τοὺς Ἰουδαίους ἀπὸ τῆς Ῥώμης προσῆλθεν αὐτοῖς καὶ διὰ τὸ ὁμότεχνον εἶναι ἔμενεν παρ’ αὐτοῖς καὶ ἠργάζετο ἦσαν γὰρ σκηνοποιοὶ τῇ τέχνῃ

passages.text: Every Sabbath he reasoned in the synagogue, trying to persuade Jews and Greeks alike.
passages.sermon:
Paul was in Corinth.
Paul went to the synagogue every Sabbath.
He spoke with the people there.
He tried to persuade both Jews and Greeks.
passages.original: Διελέγετο δὲ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον ἔπειθέν τε Ἰουδαίους καὶ Ἕλληνας

passages.text: And when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul devoted himself fully to the word, testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.
passages.sermon:
Silas and Timothy were followers of Jesus.
They came down from Macedonia.
Paul was also a follower of Jesus.
Paul began to focus completely on preaching the word of God.
Paul spoke to the Jews.
Paul told the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ κατῆλθον ἀπὸ τῆς Μακεδονίας ὅ τε Σιλᾶς καὶ ὁ Τιμόθεος συνείχετο τῷ λόγῳ ὁ Παῦλος διαμαρτυρόμενος τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις εἶναι τὸν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν

passages.text: But when they opposed and insulted him, he shook out his garments and told them, “Your blood be on your own heads! I am innocent of it. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.”
passages.sermon:
Paul preached in the synagogue.
Some Jews opposed Paul.
They insulted him.
Paul shook out his garments.
He spoke to them.
He said, "Your blood is on your own heads."
He said, "I am innocent."
He said, "From now on I will go to the Gentiles."
passages.original: ἀντιτασσομένων δὲ αὐτῶν καὶ βλασφημούντων ἐκτιναξάμενος τὰ ἱμάτια εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Τὸ αἷμα ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν ὑμῶν καθαρὸς ἐγώ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν εἰς τὰ ἔθνη πορεύσομαι

passages.text: So Paul left the synagogue and went next door to the house of Titus Justus, a worshiper of God.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian preacher.
Paul left the synagogue.
He went to the house of Titus Justus.
Titus Justus worshiped God.
His house was next to the synagogue.
passages.original: Καὶ μεταβὰς ἐκεῖθεν εἰσῆλθεν εἰς οἰκίαν τινὸς ὀνόματι Τίτου Ἰούστου σεβομένου τὸν Θεόν οὗ ἡ οἰκία ἦν συνομοροῦσα τῇ συναγωγῇ

passages.text: Crispus, the synagogue leader, and his whole household believed in the Lord. And many of the Corinthians who heard the message believed and were baptized.
passages.sermon:
Crispus led the synagogue in Corinth.
Crispus believed in the Lord.
Everyone in Crispus’s household also believed in the Lord.
Many people in Corinth heard the message about Jesus.
Many of these Corinthians believed in the Lord.
Many of these believers were baptized.
passages.original: Κρίσπος δὲ ὁ ἀρχισυνάγωγος ἐπίστευσεν τῷ Κυρίῳ σὺν ὅλῳ τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ καὶ πολλοὶ τῶν Κορινθίων ἀκούοντες ἐπίστευον καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο

passages.text: One night the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision: “Do not be afraid; keep on speaking; do not be silent.
passages.sermon:
The Lord spoke to Paul in a vision at night.
Paul was a Christian preacher.
The Lord said, “Do not be afraid.
Keep on speaking.
Do not be silent.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Κύριος ἐν νυκτὶ δι’ ὁράματος τῷ Παύλῳ Μὴ φοβοῦ ἀλλὰ λάλει καὶ μὴ σιωπήσῃς

passages.text: For I am with you and no one will lay a hand on you, because I have many people in this city.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord spoke to Paul in a vision at night.
The Lord said, “I am with you.
No one will attack you to harm you.
I have many people in this city.”
passages.original: διότι ἐγώ εἰμι μετὰ σοῦ καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐπιθήσεταί σοι τοῦ κακῶσαί σε διότι λαός ἐστί μοι πολὺς ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ

passages.text: So Paul stayed for a year and a half, teaching the word of God among the Corinthians.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul stayed in Corinth for a year and a half.
He lived among the Corinthians during this time.
Paul taught the word of God to the people in Corinth.
passages.original: Ἐκάθισεν δὲ ἐνιαυτὸν καὶ μῆνας ἓξ διδάσκων ἐν αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: While Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews coordinated an attack on Paul and brought him before the judgment seat.
passages.sermon: Gallio was the proconsul of Achaia.\r\nThe Jews acted together against Paul.\r\nThey brought Paul before the judgment seat.
passages.original: Γαλλίωνος δὲ ἀνθυπάτου ὄντος τῆς Ἀχαΐας κατεπέστησαν ὁμοθυμαδὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸ βῆμα

passages.text: “This man is persuading the people to worship God in ways contrary to the law,” they said.
passages.sermon:
The Jews accused Paul.
They spoke to Gallio, the proconsul.
They said, “This man persuades people.”
He teaches them to worship God.
He tells them to do this in ways that go against the law.
passages.original: λέγοντες ὅτι Παρὰ τὸν νόμον ἀναπείθει οὗτος τοὺς ἀνθρώπους σέβεσθαι τὸν Θεόν

passages.text: But just as Paul was about to speak, Gallio told the Jews, “If this matter involved a wrongdoing or vicious crime, O Jews, it would be reasonable for me to hear your complaint.
passages.sermon:
Gallio was the proconsul of Achaia.
Paul stood before the judgment seat.
The Jews accused Paul.
Paul was about to speak.
Gallio spoke to the Jews.
Gallio said, “O Jews, if this matter involved a wrongdoing, I would listen to you.
If this matter involved a vicious crime, I would hear your complaint.
It would be reasonable for me to consider your case.”
passages.original: Μέλλοντος δὲ τοῦ Παύλου ἀνοίγειν τὸ στόμα εἶπεν ὁ Γαλλίων πρὸς τοὺς Ἰουδαίους Εἰ μὲν ἦν ἀδίκημά τι ἢ ῥᾳδιούργημα πονηρόν ὦ Ἰουδαῖοι κατὰ λόγον ἂν ἀνεσχόμην ὑμῶν

passages.text: But since it is a dispute about words and names and your own law, settle it yourselves. I refuse to be a judge of such things.”
passages.sermon:
Gallio was the Roman governor.
Gallio spoke to the Jews.
He said, “This is a dispute about words.
This is a dispute about names.
This is a dispute about your own law.
You must settle this matter yourselves.
I do not want to be a judge of these things.”
passages.original: εἰ δὲ ζητήματά ἐστιν περὶ λόγου καὶ ὀνομάτων καὶ νόμου τοῦ καθ’ ὑμᾶς ὄψεσθε αὐτοί κριτὴς ἐγὼ τούτων οὐ βούλομαι εἶναι

passages.text: And he drove them away from the judgment seat.
passages.sermon:
Gallio was the Roman governor.
Gallio sat at the judgment seat.
Gallio spoke to the Jews.
Gallio refused to judge their dispute.
Gallio ordered the Jews to leave.
Gallio drove them away from the judgment seat.
passages.original: καὶ ἀπήλασεν αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τοῦ βήματος

passages.text: At this, the crowd seized Sosthenes the synagogue leader and beat him in front of the judgment seat. But none of this was of concern to Gallio.
passages.sermon:
Sosthenes was the leader of the synagogue.
A crowd seized Sosthenes.
They beat Sosthenes in front of the judgment seat.
Gallio was the Roman governor present at the judgment seat.
Gallio did not care about any of these events.
passages.original: Ἐπιλαβόμενοι δὲ πάντες Σωσθένην τὸν ἀρχισυνάγωγον ἔτυπτον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ βήματος καὶ οὐδὲν τούτων τῷ Γαλλίωνι ἔμελεν

passages.text: Paul remained in Corinth for quite some time before saying goodbye to the brothers. He had his head shaved in Cenchrea to keep a vow he had made, and then he sailed for Syria, accompanied by Priscilla and Aquila.
passages.sermon:
Paul was in Corinth.
He stayed there for many days.
He was with the brothers.
He said goodbye to them.
Paul sailed to Syria.
Priscilla and Aquila went with him.
Paul had made a vow.
He shaved his head in Cenchrea because of this vow.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἔτι προσμείνας ἡμέρας ἱκανὰς τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ἀποταξάμενος ἐξέπλει εἰς τὴν Συρίαν καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ Πρίσκιλλα καὶ Ἀκύλας κειράμενος ἐν Κενχρεαῖς τὴν κεφαλήν εἶχεν γὰρ εὐχήν

passages.text: When they reached Ephesus, Paul parted ways with Priscilla and Aquila. He himself went into the synagogue there and reasoned with the Jews.
passages.sermon:
Paul traveled with Priscilla and Aquila.
They arrived in Ephesus.
Paul left Priscilla and Aquila in Ephesus.
Paul went into the synagogue in Ephesus.
Paul spoke with the Jews in the synagogue.
Paul reasoned with them.
passages.original: Κατήντησαν δὲ εἰς Ἔφεσον κἀκείνους κατέλιπεν αὐτοῦ αὐτὸς δὲ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν διελέξατο τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις

passages.text: When they asked him to stay for a while longer, he declined.
passages.sermon: The Jews in Ephesus asked Paul to stay longer.\r\nPaul did not agree to stay.\r\nPaul declined their request.
passages.original: ἐρωτώντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἐπὶ πλείονα χρόνον μεῖναι οὐκ ἐπένευσεν

passages.text: But as he left, he said, “I will come back to you if God is willing.” And he set sail from Ephesus.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian apostle and missionary.
Paul prepared to leave Ephesus.
He said to the people, “I will come back to you if God is willing.”
Paul then left Ephesus by ship.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ἀποταξάμενος καὶ εἰπών Πάλιν ἀνακάμψω πρὸς ὑμᾶς τοῦ Θεοῦ θέλοντος ἀνήχθη ἀπὸ τῆς Ἐφέσου

passages.text: When Paul had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church at Jerusalem. Then he went down to Antioch.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul traveled by ship and landed at Caesarea.
Paul went up to Jerusalem.
Paul greeted the church in Jerusalem.
Paul then went down to Antioch.
passages.original: καὶ κατελθὼν εἰς Καισάρειαν ἀναβὰς καὶ ἀσπασάμενος τὴν ἐκκλησίαν κατέβη εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν

passages.text: After Paul had spent some time in Antioch, he traveled from place to place throughout the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
passages.sermon:
Paul was in Antioch.
He stayed there for some time.
After that, Paul left Antioch.
He traveled through the region of Galatia.
He also traveled through Phrygia.
Paul went from place to place.
He strengthened all the disciples.
passages.original: Καὶ ποιήσας χρόνον τινὰ ἐξῆλθεν διερχόμενος καθεξῆς τὴν Γαλατικὴν χώραν καὶ Φρυγίαν στηρίζων πάντας τοὺς μαθητάς

passages.text: Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, well versed in the Scriptures.
passages.sermon:
Apollos was a Jew.
He came from Alexandria.
He arrived in Ephesus.
Apollos spoke eloquently.
He understood the Scriptures well.
passages.original: Ἰουδαῖος δέ τις Ἀπολλῶς ὀνόματι Ἀλεξανδρεὺς τῷ γένει ἀνὴρ λόγιος κατήντησεν εἰς Ἔφεσον δυνατὸς ὢν ἐν ταῖς γραφαῖς

passages.text: He had been instructed in the way of the Lord and was fervent in spirit. He spoke and taught accurately about Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John.
passages.sermon:
Apollos was a Jew from Alexandria.
He had learned the way of the Lord.
He was passionate in spirit.
He spoke about Jesus.
He taught about Jesus with accuracy.
He knew only the baptism of John.
passages.original: οὗτος ἦν κατηχημένος τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ ζέων τῷ πνεύματι ἐλάλει καὶ ἐδίδασκεν ἀκριβῶς τὰ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐπιστάμενος μόνον τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου

passages.text: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him in and explained to him the way of God more accurately.
passages.sermon:
Apollos was a Jew from Alexandria.
He was eloquent.
He knew the Scriptures well.
He began to speak boldly in the synagogue.
Priscilla and Aquila heard Apollos speak.
They took Apollos aside.
They explained the way of God to him more accurately.
passages.original: οὗτός τε ἤρξατο παρρησιάζεσθαι ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ ἀκούσαντες δὲ αὐτοῦ Πρίσκιλλα καὶ Ἀκύλας προσελάβοντο αὐτὸν καὶ ἀκριβέστερον αὐτῷ ἐξέθεντο τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: When Apollos resolved to cross over to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples there to welcome him. On his arrival, he was a great help to those who by grace had believed.
passages.sermon:
Apollos was a Christian teacher.
He decided to go to Achaia.
The brothers encouraged Apollos.
They wrote a letter to the disciples in Achaia.
They told the disciples to welcome Apollos.
Apollos arrived in Achaia.
He helped the believers there.
These believers had received grace from God.
passages.original: Βουλομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ διελθεῖν εἰς τὴν Ἀχαΐαν προτρεψάμενοι οἱ ἀδελφοὶ ἔγραψαν τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἀποδέξασθαι αὐτόν ὃς παραγενόμενος συνεβάλετο πολὺ τοῖς πεπιστευκόσιν διὰ τῆς χάριτος

passages.text: For he powerfully refuted the Jews in public debate, proving from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.
passages.sermon:
Apollos spoke with great power.
He argued with the Jews in public.
He used the Scriptures to prove his point.
He showed that Jesus is the Christ.
passages.original: εὐτόνως γὰρ τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις διακατηλέγχετο δημοσίᾳ ἐπιδεικνὺς διὰ τῶν γραφῶν εἶναι τὸν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν
